principle: This project's ancient character asset preset uses the user-selected balanced P9 Fashion direction. Natural adult proportion remains an explicit alternative, not a forced correction of P9. Full-body anchors preserve their own proportions. Hair ornaments and trailing cloth do not count as anatomical height.

prompt_translation: Use ordinary adult studio-portrait proportions, with an approximately seven to seven-and-a-half head visual guide measured from the anatomical crown to chin, excluding hair volume and ornaments. This is a design guide, not a measurement inferred from a cropped reference.

Keep a naturally sized head, a normal neck, a complete ribcage-to-pelvis relationship and balanced upper and lower legs. Do not shrink the head, raise the anatomical waist, lengthen the neck or stretch the lower body to make the outfit look taller.

The clothing hangs over the body; its sash does not redefine the anatomical waist, and a long skirt or train does not extend the person's standing height. Keep shoulder, elbow, wrist and shoe scale coherent, without claiming hidden joints are visible.

robe_rules: Use natural waist placement and central vertical panels to preserve a tall read under long robes. Shoes may remain naturally hidden by the pose and garment.
Do not let oversized sleeves or excessive hem width suppress the lower-body visual length.
Do not shorten the torso, extreme-shrink the head, or stretch only one leg segment.
prompt_translation: Maintain a clear P9 fashion-asset proportion even under layered long robes: a coherent tall fashion silhouette, relaxed shoulders and neck, a clear natural waist and complete silhouette. Foot visibility depends on pose and clothing. Do not shrink the head extremely, stretch the neck or shift the anatomical pelvis upward.
Keep the torso anatomically complete and lengthen the lower-body impression through balanced hip-knee-ankle relationships rather than artificial leg stretching.
Control sleeve and hem width so the costume supports height instead of visually compressing it.

Balance shoulders, ribcage, waist and pelvis with a defined waist and natural hip volume. Keep upper arms, forearms, elbows, wrists and hands coherent; keep thighs, knees, calves and ankles balanced in both length and thickness. Golden proportion is an aesthetic goal, not a universal numeric ratio or a measurement inferred through clothing.

Use moderate, evenly developed muscle volume with soft definition on visible shoulders, arms, waist and legs, responding to the selected action. Preserve natural soft tissue; avoid stick limbs, pinched waists, exaggerated bodybuilding cuts or muscles showing through opaque fabric.
